chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about the dyer who spoils (the cloth). He said: 'Every worker who is given the wage on the condition that he repairs (or works properly), but then spoils, is liable (for the damage).'

key_terms.الْقَصَّارِ: The dyer (a specific type of artisan/worker)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a worker who damages an item while being paid for proper work?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on leases, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the condition of *daman* (liability) for hired workers. It establishes that compensation is contingent upon proper performance; thus, if a worker is paid to repair or maintain an item but causes damage instead, they become financially liable for the loss, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that wages are tied to the fulfillment of the specific contractual obligation.
